definition_zh: 轻视；贬低；小看；使显得渺小
definition_en: to make a person or thing seem small, unimportant, or of little value
core_image: 一根手指把一个活生生的人压成了小人国里的模型
scene: 他在会上当众把同事辛苦半年的成果说得不值一提。He kept belittling his colleague's work in front of the whole team.
sceneCN: 这里 belittling 是「贬低、小看」（第 1 个义项：使显得不重要）；句意是他当众把同事的成果说得一文不值。

derivatives.zh: 由现在分词转形容词，义为「贬低人的」

senses.title: To make someone seem unimportant
senses.definition: to speak or act as if a person or their work has little value
senses.definitionCN: 言语或行为上把人、把成果说得没什么价值
senses.example: He kept belittling his colleague's work in front of the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 他当众不断贬低同事的工作。
senses.why: Be- plus little literally makes little, so the word pictures shrinking a person by words.
senses.whyCN: be- 加 little 字面即「使变小」，词形本身就画出用言语把人缩小。

senses.title: To make something seem less serious
senses.definition: to treat a problem, danger, or effort as smaller or less serious than it is
senses.definitionCN: 把问题、危险或努力看得比实际更轻、更小
senses.example: The report belittled the risks of the new procedure.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告低估了新流程的风险。
senses.why: The same shrinking image can be applied to things, not only to people.
senses.whyCN: 「缩小」的意象同样可以施加在事物上，而不只是人。

senses.title: To modestly play down oneself
senses.definition: to speak of one's own abilities or work as less than they really are
senses.definitionCN: 把自己的能力或成果说得不如实际
senses.example: She belittles her own talent whenever anyone praises her.
senses.exampleCN: 每当有人夸她，她总是把自己的才华说得平平。
senses.why: The shrinking image can turn inward, onto oneself.
senses.whyCN: 「缩小」的意象可以转向自身，成为自谦。

intro.en: Belittle is be- plus little, an American coinage of the eighteenth century.
intro.cn: belittle 由 be- 加 little 构成，是十八世纪的美国造词。

items.en: Thomas Jefferson coined belittle in 1781-1782 in Notes on the State of Virginia.
items.cn: 托马斯·杰斐逊于 1781 至 1782 年在《弗吉尼亚笔记》中造出 belittle。

items.en: it was first used to mock European writers who belittled America.
items.cn: 最初用于讽刺那些贬低美洲的欧洲作家。

items.en: British critics at first called the word barbarous, then adopted it.
items.cn: 十九世纪英国评论家起初斥之为粗俗，后来接受了它。

items.en: the sense settled on disparaging people or their work.
items.cn: 词义逐渐固定为贬低人或其成果。

items.en: belittle now names the everyday act of talking someone down.
items.cn: 如今 belittle 专指日常中用言语把人压低。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the be- prefix or little root; the near-meaning group gathers words for putting down.
note.cn: 形近组共享 be- 前缀或 little 词基；近义组汇集贬低类动词。

entries.definitionCN: 迟来的——同用 be- 前缀，意义无关

entries.definition: to act as a friend to
entries.definitionCN: 善待——同前缀、意义几乎相反

entries.definition: to speak of as of little worth
to reduce to the smallest possible degree

normalIntro.en: Belittle is be- plus little: make little by words.
normalIntro.cn: belittle 是 be- 加 little：用言语把人变小。

normal.en: Belittle means to make someone seem small.
normal.cn: belittle 意为使人显得渺小。
过去式与过去分词是 belittled。

normal.en: It was coined by Thomas Jefferson.
Do not confuse with belief or belie.

abstract.en: See a giant finger pressing a person into a tiny model.
abstract.cn: 看一根巨指把人压成小模型。
把言语感受成缩小光线。

abstract.en: Picture a trophy melting into dust.

examples.en: He kept belittling his colleague's work in front of the whole team.
examples.cn: 他当众不断贬低同事的工作。

examples.en: The report belittled the risks of the new procedure.
examples.cn: 这份报告低估了新流程的风险。

examples.en: She belittles her own talent whenever anyone praises her.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「比·理拓」——非要跟你比，还把你的道理拓得越来越小。

root: 前缀 be-（古英语，表「使成为」）加 little（古英语 lytel「小」）；该词为 1781 至 1782 年杰斐逊在《弗吉尼亚笔记》中的创新造词，本义「使变小」，后专指用言语贬低。

sensesIntro.en: One verb shrinks people, things, or even the speaker's own worth.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个动词，把人、把事、甚至把自己的价值都「缩小」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger pressing a person into a tiny model.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指把人压成小模型。

intro.en: Belittle shows be- turning little into a verb.
intro.cn: belittle 展示 be- 把 little 变成动词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; both parts are English.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，两部分均为英语成分。
